blocks.text:
Workplace & Professional Communication
เป้าหมาย: สื่อสารปัญหางานพร้อมผลกระทบ ทางเลือก และผู้รับผิดชอบ

Use the language of workplace & professional communication to complete the unit's practical or interpretive task.
Identify and relay the essential information in the two readings without adding unsupported facts.
Respond to the two listening scripts with appropriate clarification and source-sensitive wording.

Reading A
A project team learns that a supplier will deliver display panels two days later than expected. The exhibition date is fixed, so the coordinator sends a concise update. She states what is confirmed, explains the effect on installation and offers two options: use temporary panels or reduce the display area. She asks the design lead to assess presentation quality and the venue manager to check access. She does not hide the delay behind vague language such as 'some challenges have arisen.' The message ends with a decision deadline and the person responsible for collecting replies. Clear professional communication makes action possible without assigning blame before the facts are known.

Read for purpose, then locate the people, events, conditions and limits. Map claim, supporting evidence, alternative explanation and limitation. Compare sources on the same question. Build a proportionate conclusion and address a fair counterargument. Explain why your evidence supports a claim rather than merely repeating it.

Reading B
Update extract: Supplier confirms delivery on Wednesday, not Monday. Installation access ends Thursday at 17:00. Please assess temporary panels by Tuesday noon. Noor will consolidate responses; the project lead will decide that afternoon. Costs remain provisional.

Compare the two inputs: what is shared, what is additional, and what is not known? Use only details actually supplied. All characters, organisations, figures and events in these inputs are fictional classroom materials.

future arrangements and deadlines
หน้าที่: เชื่อมงานกับเวลา
Model: The lead will decide on Tuesday afternoon.
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

หน้าที่: ไม่รับรองข้อมูลที่ยังไม่แน่
Model: Costs may change after assessment.

Guided practice: cover the word bank, reconstruct five target expressions, and explain their meaning in these particular contexts. Then use two in a new example. The same word may have a different sense elsewhere.

Listening script A — authored script; recorded audio and human audio QC are pending. Reading the transcript is text-based preparation, not evidence of independent listening ability.

A: Should we tell the client everything is under control?
B: We can say what we have confirmed and what options we are checking.
A: Who makes the final decision?
B: The project lead, after the design and access checks.
A: I'll make the deadline explicit.

Listening script B
A useful update distinguishes facts, risks, actions and owners. State the decision needed and when it is needed. If an estimate is provisional, label it. Avoid promises that depend on approvals or information you do not yet have.

First pass: identify purpose and main message. Second pass: note essential details and any corrections. Check against the script only after the listening attempt when approved audio becomes available. For now, practise with a teacher or partner reading the script.

Pronunciation and prosody
Use prominence to distinguish your position from a reported view. Pause at changes of argument. Signal concession and contrast with phrasing, without relying on exaggerated stress to make weak evidence sound stronger.

Interaction rehearsal: take both roles. Ask one clarification question, answer it using the source, and check that the other person has understood. Do not equate quietness, accent or hesitation with lack of ability.

Unit transfer task
สื่อสารปัญหางานพร้อมผลกระทบ ทางเลือก และผู้รับผิดชอบ

Prepare a 180–240-word response and a 120–180-second spoken response using the unit inputs. Develop sustained positions, evaluate competing practical options and relay complex information with clear qualification.

Planning sequence
1. Identify audience and purpose.
2. Select source details that the audience needs.
3. Mark any uncertainty, unconfirmed arrangement or missing information.
4. Choose two language features from Lesson 2.
5. Produce the response, then check meaning before surface accuracy.

Mediation: explain the essential information to a Thai-speaking classmate who has not read the sources. Preserve dates, quantities, conditions, agency and uncertainty. Say what cannot be concluded.

Online interaction: respond to a request for clarification, then add a follow-up checking question. Acknowledge corrections and revise your message where needed.

Quick review

active responsibility: Noor will consolidate responses.

pronunciation: Use prominence to distinguish your position from a reported view. Pause at changes of argument. Signal concession and contrast with phrasing, without relying on exaggerated stress to make weak evidence sound stronger.

rubric.descriptors:
Target B2: Develop sustained positions, evaluate competing practical options and relay complex information with clear qualification.
4 — Fully achieves the specified purpose with precise relevant detail, coherent organisation and effective control at this target level.
3 — Achieves the main purpose; minor omissions or language lapses do not materially distort meaning.
2 — Partially achieves the purpose; important detail, organisation or language needs revision.
1 — Limited assessable evidence; major gaps or distortion impede the task.
0 — No assessable response or wholly unrelated response.
Rate each dimension separately. For mediation, invented facts, erased conditions or reversed agency prevent a high fidelity score. Do not penalise an accent or a defensible alternative phrasing. Scores describe this task only, not certified CEFR attainment.

retrieval.prompt: Without notes: recall 2 target expressions from Workplace & Professional Communication; explain one source detail and use future arrangements and deadlines in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.

Without notes: recall 3 target expressions from Workplace & Professional Communication; explain one source detail and use active responsibility in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.
Without notes: recall 4 target expressions from Workplace & Professional Communication; explain one source detail and use provisional modality in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.

Without notes: recall 5 target expressions from Workplace & Professional Communication; explain one source detail and use future arrangements and deadlines in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.

remediation.action: Return to Readings A/B; underline the evidence for your statement, restore any lost condition, and say explicitly what remains unknown. Retry Q-B2-07-015 and the mediation task.
Revisit the three Lesson 2 models. Identify the intended function, correct the form, and produce a new example. Retrieve the missed expression again after one day.

masteryCheck.decision: Record evidence by construct; no pass mark or CEFR certification without human standard setting.

{
  "id": "B2-07",
  "aim": "สื่อสารปัญหางานพร้อมผลกระทบ ทางเลือก และผู้รับผิดชอบ",
  "a": "A project team learns that a supplier will deliver display panels two days later than expected. The exhibition date is fixed, so the coordinator sends a concise update. She states what is confirmed, explains the effect on installation and offers two options: use temporary panels or reduce the display area. She asks the design lead to assess presentation quality and the venue manager to check access. She does not hide the delay behind vague language such as 'some challenges have arisen.' The message ends with a decision deadline and the person responsible for collecting replies. Clear professional communication makes action possible without assigning blame before the facts are known.",
  "b": "Update extract: Supplier confirms delivery on Wednesday, not Monday. Installation access ends Thursday at 17:00. Please assess temporary panels by Tuesday noon. Noor will consolidate responses; the project lead will decide that afternoon. Costs remain provisional.",
  "l1": "A: Should we tell the client everything is under control?\nB: We can say what we have confirmed and what options we are checking.\nA: Who makes the final decision?\nB: The project lead, after the design and access checks.\nA: I'll make the deadline explicit.",
  "l2": "A useful update distinguishes facts, risks, actions and owners. State the decision needed and when it is needed. If an estimate is provisional, label it. Avoid promises that depend on approvals or information you do not yet have.",
  "v": "supplier=ผู้จัดหา;display panels=แผงจัดแสดง;coordinator=ผู้ประสานงาน;concise=กระชับ;installation=การติดตั้ง;temporary=ชั่วคราว;assess=ประเมิน;venue=สถานที่จัดงาน;vague=คลุมเครือ;deadline=เส้นตาย;consolidate=รวบรวมเป็นชุด;provisional=ยังไม่ยืนยัน;explicit=ชัดแจ้ง;owners=ผู้รับผิดชอบงาน;approvals=การอนุมัติ",
  "g": [
    [
      "future arrangements and deadlines",
      "เชื่อมงานกับเวลา",
      "The lead will decide on Tuesday afternoon."
    ],
    [
      "active responsibility",
      "ระบุเจ้าของงาน",
      "Noor will consolidate responses."
    ],
    [
      "provisional modality",
      "ไม่รับรองข้อมูลที่ยังไม่แน่",
      "Costs may change after assessment."
    ]
  ],
  "q": [
    [
      "How late is the delivery?",
      "two days",
      "a"
    ],
    [
      "What are the two proposed options?",
      "temporary panels or a reduced display area",
      "a"
    ],
    [
      "When are assessments due?",
      "Tuesday noon",
      "b"
    ],
    [
      "Who makes the final decision?",
      "the project lead",
      "l1"
    ]
  ]
}
